How the Telephone Talks is a 1919 American silent educational documentary film made by Bray Studios. It demonstrates how the telephone works with a series of demonstrations and animated diagrams. The film was released on April 27, 1919.
Solomon in Society is a 1922 American silent drama film directed by Lawrence C. Windom and starring Charles Delaney and Lillian Herlein.
Bag and Baggage is a 1923 American silent comedy film directed by Finis Fox and starring Gloria Grey, John Roche and Carmelita Geraghty.
I Am the Man is a 1924 American silent drama film directed by Ivan Abramson and starring Lionel Barrymore, Seena Owen, and Gaston Glass.
Getting 'Em Right is a 1925 American silent action film, directed by Jack Harvey. It stars George Larkin, Jane Thomas, and Ollie Kirkby.
The Grey Devil is a 1926 American silent Western film directed by Bennett Cohen and starring Jack Perrin, Lorraine Eason and Tom London.
The Fighting Hombre is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Jack Nelson and starring Bob Custer, Mary O'Day and Bert Sprotte.
The Flying U Ranch is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Robert De Lacey and starring Tom Tyler, Nora Lane and Bert Hadley.
Skedaddle Gold is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Richard Thorpe and starring Hal Taliaferro, Betty Baker and Bob Burns.
The Devil's Tower is a 1928 American silent western film directed by J.P. McGowan and starring Buddy Roosevelt, Thelma Parr and McGowan.
Destiny is a 1915 American silent drama film directed by Edwin Carewe and starring Emily Stevens, George Le Guere and Walter Hitchcock.
Tainted Money is a 1924 American silent drama film directed by Henry MacRae and starring William Fairbanks, Eva Novak and Bruce Gordon.
Women First is a 1924 American silent drama film directed by B. Reeves Eason and starring William Fairbanks, Eva Novak and Lydia Knott.
Danger Quest is a 1926 American silent action film directed by Harry Joe Brown and starring Reed Howes, Ethel Shannon and J.P. McGowan.
The Impostor is a 1926 American silent crime film directed by Chester Withey and starring Evelyn Brent, Carroll Nye and James Morrison.
Hard Fists is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by William Wyler and starring Art Acord, Louise Lorraine and Gilbert Holmes.
No Place to Go is a 1927 American silent romance film directed by Mervyn LeRoy and starring Mary Astor, Lloyd Hughes and Hallam Cooley.
Western Courage is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Ben Wilson, starring Richard Hatton, Elsa Benham, and Robert Walker.
Wolf's Trail is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Francis Ford and starring Edmund Cobb, Dixie Lamont and Joseph Bennett.
The Bride of the Colorado is a 1928 American silent romantic drama film directed by Elmer Clifton starring John Boles and Rose Blossom.
Manhattan Cowboy is a 1928 American silent Western film directed by J.P. McGowan and starring Bob Custer, Lafe McKee and Mary Mayberry.
Silent Trail is a 1928 American silent Western film directed by J.P. McGowan and starring Bob Custer, Peggy Montgomery and John Lowell.
The Body in the Trunk is a 1914 American silent short drama film directed by John O' Brien starring William Garwood and George Larkin.
The Empress is a 1917 American silent drama film directed by Alice Guy and starring Doris Kenyon, Holbrook Blinn and William A. Morse.
Don't Shoot is a 1922 American silent crime film directed by Jack Conway and starring Herbert Rawlinson, Edna Murphy and Harvey Clark.
The Enchanted Cottage is a 1924 American silent drama film directed by John S. Robertson based upon a 1923 play by Arthur Wing Pinero.
The Taming of the West is a lost 1925 American silent Western film directed by Arthur Rosson and starring top cowboy star Hoot Gibson.
Thrilling Youth is a 1926 American silent comedy film directed by Grover Jones and starring Billy West, Gloria Grey and Charles Clary.
Daring Deeds is a 1927 American silent comedy film directed by Duke Worne and starring Billy Sullivan, Molly Malone and Earl Metcalfe.
A Man's Past is a 1927 American silent drama film directed by George Melford and starring Conrad Veidt, Barbara Bedford and Ian Keith.
Road House is a 1928 American silent drama film directed by Richard Rosson and starring Maria Alba, Warren Burke and Lionel Barrymore.
Trail Riders is a 1928 American silent Western film directed by J.P. McGowan and starring Buddy Roosevelt, Lafe McKee and Betty Baker.
Wild Blood is a 1928 American silent Western film directed by Henry MacRae and starring Jack Perrin, Ethlyne Clair and Theodore Lorch.
Calamity Anne's Inheritance is a 1913 American silent short Western film directed by Allan Dwan. It stars Louise Lester as Calamity Anne, with J. Warren Kerrigan and Charlotte Burton.
The Test is a 1916 American silent drama film directed by George Fitzmaurice and starring Jane Grey, Lumsden Hare and Claude Fleming.
That Sort is a 1916 American silent drama film directed by Charles Brabin and starring Warda Howard, Duncan McRae and Ernest Maupain.
Over the Hill is a 1917 American silent drama film directed by William Parke and starring Gladys Hulette, J.H. Gilmour and Dan Mason.
The Truth About Women is a lost 1924 American silent film drama directed by Burton King and starring Hope Hampton and Lowell Sherman.
The Red Rider is a 1925 American silent Western film directed by Clifford Smith. It is not known whether the film currently survives.
Desert Dust is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by William Wyler and starring Ted Wells, Lotus Thompson and Bruce Gordon.
Range Courage is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Ernst Laemmle and starring Fred Humes, Gloria Grey and Dick Winslow.
Speeding Hoofs is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Louis Chaudet and starring Dick Hatton, Elsa Benham and Ray Turner.
Speedy Smith is a 1927 American silent drama film directed by Duke Worne and starring Billy Sullivan, Hazel Deane and Harry Tenbrook.
The Swell-Head is a 1927 American silent drama film directed by Ralph Graves and starring Graves, Johnnie Walker and Eugenia Gilbert.
Sunday is a 1915 American silent drama film directed by George W. Lederer and starring Reine Davies, Montagu Love and Barney McPhee.
The Broken Cross is a 1916 American silent short romantic film directed by Thomas Ricketts starring Harold Lockwood and May Allison.
The Magic Eye is a 1918 American silent drama film directed by Rae Berger and starring Henry A. Barrows, Claire Du Brey and Zoe Rae.
Kicking the Germ Out of Germany is a 1918 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. The film is now considered a lost film.
Western Pluck is a 1926 American silent Western film directed by Travers Vale and starring Art Acord, Marceline Day, and Ray Ripley.
The Boy Rider is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Louis King and starring Buzz Barton, Lorraine Eason and Sam Nelson.
Face Value is a 1927 American silent drama film directed by Robert Florey and starring Fritzi Ridgeway, Gene Gowing and Betty Baker.
Driftwood is a 1928 American silent drama film directed by Christy Cabanne and starring Don Alvarado, Marceline Day and Alan Roscoe.
Samson, an Israelite whose enormous strength is legendary, falls in love with Zorah, a Philistine, and marries her, overcoming his father Manoah's objections.
Coral is a 1915 American silent drama film directed by Henry MacRae and starring Marie Walcamp, Wellington A. Playter and Ruby Cox.
Babette is a 1917 American silent drama film directed by Charles Brabin and starring Marc McDermott, Peggy Hyland and Templar Saxe.
Painted Lips is a 1918 American silent drama film directed by Edward LeSaint and starring Louise Lovely, Alfred Allen and Lew Cody.
Loyal Lives is a 1923 American silent drama film directed by Charles Giblyn and starring Brandon Tynan, Mary Carr and Faire Binney.
Lazy Lightning is a 1926 American silent Western film directed by William Wyler and starring Art Acord, Fay Wray and Robert Gordon.
Texas Tommy is a 1928 American silent Western film directed by J.P. McGowan and starring Bob Custer, Mary Mayberry and Bud Osborne.
Young Whirlwind is a 1928 American silent Western film directed by Louis King and starring Buzz Barton, Edmund Cobb and Frank Rice.
All for a Girl is a 1912 American short silent film romantic comedy, directed by Frederick A. Thomson and written by Wallace Reid.
The Lure of Heart's Desire is a 1916 silent American drama film directed by Francis J. Grandon. The film is considered to be lost.
Honor Among Men is a 1924 American silent film directed by Denison Clift and starring Edmund Lowe, Claire Adams and Sheldon Lewis.
Duty's Reward is a 1927 American silent drama film directed by Bertram Bracken and starring Alan Roscoe, Eva Novak and Lou Archer.
Put 'Em Up is a 1928 American silent Western film directed by Edgar Lewis and starring Fred Humes, Gloria Grey and Gilbert Holmes.
The Englishman and the Girl was a 1910 short comedy film directed by D. W. Griffith. Being restored by Film Preservation Society.
Her Younger Sister is a 1914 American silent short drama film directed by Frank Cooley starring Fred Gamble and Charlotte Burton.
Divorce is a 1923 American silent drama film directed by Chester Bennett and starring Jane Novak, John Bowers and James Corrigan.
Rich Men's Sons is a 1927 American silent drama film directed by Ralph Graves and starring Graves, Shirley Mason and Robert Cain.
Calamity Anne's Vanity is a 1913 American silent short Western film directed by Allan Dwan. It stars Louise Lester as Calamity Anne, with J. Warren Kerrigan and Charlotte Burton.
A Jewel in Pawn is a 1917 American silent drama film directed by Jack Conway and starring Ella Hall, Maie Hall and Antrim Short.
Harold becomes the victim of a clever bulldog pup who chases him in and out of various places.
Hoof Marks is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Tenny Wright and starring Jack Donovan, Ed Brady and Edward Cecil.
The Range Riders is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Ben F. Wilson and starring Wilson, Neva Gerber, Al Ferguson.
Swing Your Partners is a 1918 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. Copies of the film survive in two collections.
Sacred Silence is a 1919 American silent drama film directed by Harry F. Millarde and starring William Russell and Agnes Ayres.
Crack Your Heels is a 1919 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd.
Mistaken Orders is a 1925 silent film action adventure directed by J. P. McGowan. It starred Helen Holmes and Henry A. Barrows.
The Scarlet Letter (1911) is a silent drama motion picture short starring King Baggot, Lucille Young, and William Robert Daly.
An Enemy to the King is a 1916 silent film directed by Frederick A. Thomson.
Mentioned in Confidence is a 1917 silent film drama directed by Edgar Jones and produced by the Balboa Film Producing Company.
Chop Suey & Co. is a 1919 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd.
Harold is a henpecked husband who suddenly makes a change of front and asserts himself, much to his wife's astonishment.
Blazing Days is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by William Wyler and produced and released by Universal Pictures.
The Big Idea is a 1917 American short comedy film starring Harold Lloyd. The film has been preserved and is available online.
Ace High is a 1918 American silent Western film directed by Lynn Reynolds and starring Tom Mix, Lloyd Perl and Lewis Sargent.
The Big Catch is a 1920 American short silent Western film released by the Universal Film Mfg. Co., written by Ford Beebe, directed by Leo D. Maloney and starring Hoot Gibson.
The Tigress is a 1927 American silent drama film directed by George B. Seitz. The film is currently believed to be lost film.

String Whalen, a carnival wheel-of-fortune operator, is greatly attracted to Lutie and gains her gratitude when he recovers her purse from a pickpocket. At a dance that evening, String promises Lutie to forsake his gambling career.
Never Touched Me is a 1919 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. A print exists in the Staatliches Filmarchive.
A Gamblin' Fool is a 1920 American short silent Western film released by Universal Film Mfg. Co., written by Ford Beebe, directed by Leo D. Maloney and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The Sheriff's Oath is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by Phil Rosen and featuring Hoot Gibson. The film was produced and distributed by Universal Pictures.
Give and Take is a lost 1928 American silent comedy film directed by William Beaudine. It was Universal's second sound film.
The Light at Dusk is a lost 1916 silent film drama directed by Edgar Lewis and produced by the Lubin Manufacturing Company.
The Proof of the Man is a 1913 American silent short drama film starring Alexander Gaden, Harry von Meter and Edna Maison.
Under False Colors is a 1917 American silent drama film produced by the Thanhouser Company and directed by Emile Chautard.
The Leech is a 1921 American silent drama film directed by Herbert Hancock and starring Alexander Hall and Claire Whitney.
Two Outlaws is a 1928 American silent Western film directed by Henry MacRae and starring Jack Perrin and Kathleen Collins.
Silent Sentinel is a 1929 American silent crime film directed by Alan James and starring Gareth Hughes and Josephine Hill.
The Trail of the Hound is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by Albert Russell and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The Passing of Wolf MacLean is a 1924 silent Western film directed by Paul Hurst and produced by and starring Jack Mower.

Arrival of Tongkin Train, also referred to as Arrival of Train, Tien-Tsin, is a 1901 documentary silent film showing the arrival of a train in Tianjin, China. The film was made by American Mutoscope and Biograph Company.
Law of Fear is a 1928 American silent western film directed by Jerome Storm and starring Sam Nelson and Albert J. Smith.
The Lookout Girl is a surviving 1928 silent film mystery directed by Dallas M. Fitzgerald and starring Jacqueline Logan.
The Sky Rider is a 1928 American silent drama film directed by Alan James and starring Gareth Hughes and Josephine Hill.
Home Struck is a 1927 American silent film directed by Ralph Ince and starring Viola Dana, Alan Brooks and Tom Gallery.
Standing Room Only is a 1912 American silent short romantic comedy film starring William Garwood, and Mignon Anderson.
In the Open is a 1914 American silent short film directed by Sydney Ayres, starring William Garwood and Louise Lester.
A Sanitarium Scramble is a 1916 American short comedy film produced by the American Film Manufacturing Company, released by Mutual Film and directed by B. Reeves Eason.
The Royal Pauper is a 1917 silent film starring Francine Larrimore and Richard Tucker. It was directed by Ben Turbett.
Lonesome Luke on Tin Can Alley is a 1917 American short comedy film starring Harold Lloyd. A print of the film survives in the film archive of the Museum of Modern Art.
True Nobility is a 1916 American silent drama directed by Donald MacDonald starring Helene Rosson and Forrest Taylor.
Traveling from the Latin Quarter of Paris to Brittany to seek inspiration for his painting, artist Paul Dachette finds it in the person of Mignon, an orphan who consents to pose for him.
Campus on the March is a short propaganda film produced by the Office of War Information in 1942.
The Old Bookkeeper is a 1912 American short silent drama film directed by D. W. Griffith and starring Blanche Sweet.
A Society Sherlock is a 1916 American silent short comedy directed by and starring William Garwood and Irma Dawkins.

So This is Love? was another early Frank Capra production for fledgling Columbia Pictures. The hero, dress designer Jerry McGuire (William Collier Jr.), is tired of being considered a wimp. After business hours, Jerry secretly takes boxing lessons, enabling him to knock the stuffings out of his burly rival Spike Mullins (Johnnie Walker). Jerry's newfound pugilistic skills wins him the affections of store clerk Hilda Jensen (Shirley Mason), who's just car-razy about "cave men." Filmed in a fast three weeks, So This is Love? was completed before Frank Capra's Matinee Idol but released afterward.
The Tell-Tale Message is a 1912 American short silent film drama.
Cupid in a Dental Parlor is a 1913 American short comedy film directed by Henry Lehrman. Harold Lloyd is said to have appeared in this film, but this is unconfirmed.

A ranchman sets fire to his trousers with a cigarette. In the morning the hotel attendant furnishes him with a pair borrowed from a cattle rustler. A note in one of the pockets gets the hero into trouble, but he clears himself and wins the girl of his choice.
Dog Law is a 1928 American silent action film directed by Jerome Storm and starring Jules Cowles and Mary Mayberry.
The Bigger Man is a lost 1915 silent film drama directed by John W. Noble and starring Henry Kolker, a stage star.

Ruth Minchin is unhappily married to her father's former business partner, a drunken brute. She contracts a friendship for Severino, a pianist, who lives in the same apartment house, and Minchin, discovering them together, orders the pianist from the room and knocks his wife down. Severino kills Minchin in a delirium following pneumonia, and Ruth is suspected of the crime.
A schoolteacher helps his friend Dora by getting his students to help him to make a radio commercial.

John Hampstead gives up his career as an actor and his actress sweetheart, Marian Dounay, to become a minister in a western town. Marian appears, and failing to win him back she tries to ruin his reputation. Hampstead is accused of stealing some jewelry though actually he is protecting the scapegrace brother of his current sweetheart, Bessie.
The Hindoo Dagger is a 1909 American Short film and Mystery Drama directed by D. W. Griffith and the film was made by the American Mutoscope and Biograph Company.
Luke, stranded on a desert island, becomes chief of the natives. When he pursues the affections of a pretty white girl, he runs afoul of her sweetheart and has to swim back home.
The Substitute Wife is a 1925 American silent drama film written by Katherine Smith and directed by Wilfred Noy.
Wood for War was a 1942 color short produced by the United States Department of Agriculture.
A woman goes to the dentist for a toothache and is given gas. On her way home on the subway she can't stop laughing, and every other passenger catches the laughter from her.
The Voice of Conscience is a 1912 American silent short drama film starring Florence La Badie and Jean Darnell.

Our newlywed hero is about to embark on a journey when he realizes that he has lost the train tickets. A crook knocks him down and switches clothes with him. The assailant's victims pursue our man while his bride is led to believe that she has been deserted.
Luke and the Bang-Tails is a 1916 American short comedy film starring Harold Lloyd. A print of the film survives in the film archive of the Museum of Modern Art.
Adventuress Stefanie Paoli forsakes her lover, humble fisherman Gabriel Barrato, for the arms of a nobleman, the Marquis de Mohrivart.

During World War I, Francine D'Espard, a young French woman, meets William Holliday, a U.S. Army officer at the front, and they become engaged. Returning to America, William finds his father at the mercy of his business rival, Ezekiel Bates. Shortly after, when Francine arrives in America to marry her fiancé, she is informed that her lover is about to marry Bates's daughter Susan. Her love now turning to hate, Francine devotes herself to the task of destroying her former suitor.
Documentary short film demonstrating methods used by the War Manpower Commission to resolve problems in worker shortages.

The 957th Day was a propaganda short produced by the US Navy in 1944. The film uses authentic battle footage of the taking of Guam on July 21, 1944, and one narration follows the battle chronologically, while another narration mimics a radio news caster voice.
The Joneses Have Amateur Theatricals is a 1909 silent short comedy film directed by D. W. Griffith. It was released in split-reel form with The Hindoo Dagger.
The Solution to the Mystery is a 1915 short film produced by the American Film Manufacturing Company, released by Mutual Film and directed by B. Reeves Eason.
Easy Money is a 1925 silent film directed by Albert S. Rogell and starring Cullen Landis and Mildred Harris.
Luke Joins the Navy is a 1916 American short comedy film starring Harold Lloyd. A print of the film survives in the film archive of the Museum of Modern Art.
Josephine is called to her Western home from an Eastern college and brings a party of girls with her, accompanied by one man.
Beyond All Odds is a 1926 American silent Western film directed by Alan James and starring Eileen Sedgwick.
Deuce High is a 1926 American silent Western film directed by Richard Thorpe and starring Buffalo Bill Jr..
It Happened Thus is a 1912 American silent short romantic drama starring Charlotte Burton and Owen Moore.
The "Black Hound" band of desperadoes abduct a candidate for governor and demand a heavy ransom for him, but the hero and the girl lead a successful rescue party.
Free Lips is a 1928 silent film mystery drama directed by actor Wallace MacDonald. It stars June Marlowe.
A farce involving an esteemed judge, his young wife, and the District Attorney she's seeing on the side; Misplaced jewelry and a message written on a mirror lead to the DA's undoing.
Young Mr. Jazz is a 1919 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. A print of the film survives in the film archive of the Museum of Modern Art.
Giving Them Fits is a 1915 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. It was the first film to team up Lloyd with Snub Pollard and Bebe Daniels.
To Melody a Soul Responds is a 1915 short film produced by American Film Manufacturing Company, released by Mutual Film and directed by B. Reeves Eason.

Ruth Travers, the young niece and ward of Howard Mason, elopes with Chadwick Blake to escape the advances of Gilbert Hilton, whom her uncle wants to force upon her to cover his embezzlement of Ruth's small fortune. She discovers too late that Blake already has a wife but makes the best of the situation until Mason's death, just after he has made a lucky gambling coup, leaves her a little money. Determined to escape, she goes to a small town where minister Daniel Clarkson becomes interested in her. Because James Lawton had sought marriage between Clarkson and his daughter, when Blake turns up, and Lawton learns the story, he denounces Ruth to the minister.
Roaring Lions at Home is a 1924 short comedy film directed by American director Benjamin Stoloff. It was released by Fox Film and starred Oliver Hardy.
Who Was the Man? is a 1921 American short silent Western film directed by Lee Kohlmar, released by Universal Film Mfg. Co. and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The Gambling Fool is a 1925 silent Western film directed by J. P. McGowan starring Franklyn Farnum.

While patrolling his New York City beat, Sgt. Tim Maloney is knocked out by the Dalton gang, which was about to pull a robbery when he came along. They pour a bottle of whiskey over his unconscious body, then commit the robbery. When Maloney wakes up, still groggy from being knocked out, he stumbles out into the street, and the combination of his grogginess and the smell of whiskey leads to him being charged with being drunk on duty. He must clear his name and bring the criminal gang to justice.
The Flirt and the Bandit is a 1913 American silent short drama film directed by Lorimer Johnston starring R.D. Armstrong, Charlotte Burton, Ed Coxen, George Field, James Harrison and Chester Withey.

A British army officer refuses to avenge the death of a general who was murdered years earlier. He is awarded three feathers by his officers. When his fiancée fails to defend his stance, he plucks a feather from her fan. He proves his courage by rescuing his comrades in dangerous and life-threatening situations. Later he returns each feather as proof of his redemption and courage.
Lonesome Luke Leans to the Literary is a 1916 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd.
The Rajah is a 1919 American short comedy film directed by Hal Roach and starring Harold Lloyd.
A Fool's Revenge is a 1909 American silent short drama film directed by D. W. Griffith. It is based on the 1832 Victor Hugo play Le roi s'amuse.
The Sleeping Sentinel is a 1914 American black-and-white silent film that depicted President Abraham Lincoln pardoning a military sentry who had been sentenced to die for sleeping while on duty.

To a reception there is invited a celebrated professor of hypnotism, and during the evening he obliges with an exhibition of his wonderful powers. Several of the guests are put under the influence and made to perform most ridiculous antics, to their embarrassment upon reviving. The daughter of the host is the last to be subjected to the professor's power, and she proves to be such a good subject that the professor at once resolves to make her his unconscious agent in a dastardly plot he at once evolves.
Pride of the Range is a 1910 American short silent Western film directed by Francis Boggs. It features Hoot Gibson in his first on-screen role.
I'm on My Way is a 1919 short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. A print of the film survives in the film archive of the Museum of Modern Art.
Superstition is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by Edward Laemmle for the Universal Film Mfg. Co. and featuring Hoot Gibson.
His Ward's Love is a 1909 American Short film directed by D. W. Griffith and the film was made by the American Mutoscope and Biograph Company.
Calamity Anne's Beauty is a 1913 American silent short Western comedy film directed by Allan Dwan and starring Louise Lester as Calamity Anne.
Barnyard Flirtations is a 1914 American short comedy film directed by and starring Fatty Arbuckle. It was Arbuckle's first film as a director.
Spit-Ball Sadie is a 1915 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. It was Lloyd's first appearance as his "Lonesome Luke" character.
Chicken Chaser is a 1914 American short comedy film directed by and starring Fatty Arbuckle.
In Trust is a 1915 American short film directed by B. Reeves Eason and starring Vivian Rich.
The Jack of Hearts is a 1919 American short silent Western film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
The Tell Tale Wire is a 1919 American short silent Western film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
Snow White is a silent movie made in 1902. It was the first time the classic 1812 Brothers Grimm fairy tale was made into a film. It was registered for United States copyright on May 1, 1903.
The Fighting Line is a 1919 American short silent Western film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
Harold is a bookkeeper who works in an office but can't keep his mind on his job -- the spring weather is too nice to stay indoors. After escaping from his office he romps in the park instead.

An unscrupulous tourist plots to steal the famous diamond, "The Light of the World," tricking a young woman into helping him. She is caught and imprisoned, while he prepares to sell the diamond and make his getaway.
Luke Locates the Loot is a 1916 American short comedy film starring Harold Lloyd. A print of the film survives in the BFI National Archive.

Young reporter Jay Walker is given the job of investigating Ducket Nelson, an infamous bandit. While driving in the country Walker is held up by Nelson--who is disguised as an elderly Gypsy woman--and when his colleagues at the newspaper find out and ridicule him, his publisher tells him not to come back until he himself captures Nelson. Determined to avenge his embarrassment, he sets out to find and bring in the bandit.

Old man Wilson is much inclined to a liberal use of liquor. His daughter. Nell, is known and liked by all the cowboys of the surrounding ranches. Jack Harding is especially fond of Nell. Old man Wilson fears Jack. The manager of the ranch on which Jack works is negotiating with a livestock exchange relative to the sale of a bunch of horses, and accordingly, the buyer of the exchange, Neal Banning, arrives on the ground, accompanied by his daughter, to look over the stock. Jack finds the city-bred girl very fascinating, while she finds much to admire in the young cowboy. The two take many rides together, in which Jack explains the country and the business of the livestock people to the girl.
Luke opens a circus, but when local officials discover that his side-show attractions are fakes, trouble ensues.
Not for Publication is a 1927 American silent film directed by and starring Ralph Ince.

A gang of lawless freebooters who terrorized the country and made travel in the mountains a hazardous pastime hold up a stylish landau in which are seated an old gentleman, a duenna, and a pretty young Senora. The inevitable happens; all are relieved of their valuables, and while the gentleman and duenna are sent on their way, the girl is held a prisoner.
The Fatal Glass of Beer is a 1916 American short comedy film directed by Tod Browning.
Luke, the Candy Cut-Up is a 1916 American short comedy film starring Harold Lloyd. A print of the film survives in George Eastman House.
The Champion Liar is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by and starring Hoot Gibson for Universal Film Manufacturing Co.
Clowns Spinning Hats is a black-and-white silent film featuring clowns throwing hats back and forth to each other. It was written and produced by Lubin Films and released April 7, 1900.
The Railroad Builder is a 1911 American silent short drama film. The film starred William Garwood, Marguerite Snow and William Russell.
Luke is a movie actor who falls asleep and dreams that he and his fellow actors are school children again.
The Valley of Hell is a 1927 American silent Western film directed by Clifford Smith.
Love, Laughs and Lather is a 1917 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd.
We Never Sleep is a 1917 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. It was Lloyd's last film as his "Lonesome Luke" character.
His Chum the Baron is a 1913 American short comedy film. Harold Lloyd is said to have appeared in this film, but this is unconfirmed.

Sourball Joe gets the "can" for sassing the tenants, and Easy Otis supplants him. But the latter does not know an awful lot of the art of "janitoring" and soon gets into many and various jams with the people upstairs.

Polly Biggs helps care for her younger brother and sisters, while her widowed mother works hard as a seamstress to earn a living. Mayor Hoadley, Mrs. Biggs' brother, a crooked politician, calls to sympathize with her on the death of her husband, and Polly takes a dislike to him.
Three Weeks in Paris is a 1925 silent movie from Warner Bros. starring Matt Moore and Dorothy Devore. No copies are known to survive.
One Touch of Nature is a 1909 American silent short drama film directed by D. W. Griffith. It is not known whether the film currently survives, which suggests that it is a lost film.
The Crow is a 1919 American short silent Western film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
Willie Runs the Park is a 1915 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd.
Lonesome Luke's Wild Women is a 1917 American short comedy film starring Harold Lloyd. A print of the film exists in a collection.
Our hero, a professor in Turkey, challenges a Sultan for the affections of a girl.
Luke, running a chili parlor, inherits a million dollars and joins high society.
A rich man's daughter has more suitors than she's interested in, and he's going to marry her off -- even if she doesn't know about it.

When Silent Sanderson's brother kills himself over the rejection of a woman, Silent blames Judith Benson and leaves the family homestead to begin a new life in Alaska. He is later reunited with Judith Benson, only to discover that his brother didn't commit suicide at all but was murdered by the woman's jealous husband.
Fool's Luck is a 1926 American silent comedy film directed by Roscoe Arbuckle.
Move On is a 1917 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. A print survives in the Museum of Modern Art film archive.

Robert Ware takes it upon himself to tame wild girl, Mag, to prove to his doubting friend Arnold, he can turn her into a graceful young lady. Later, when Arnold is in the war, he meets a pretty nurse who greatly impresses him. Back home he recalls the pleasant encounter to Robert, telling him of the gentle beauty he never forgot. Mag, now Margaret, overhears the story and reveals to Arnold, she was the nurse. The surprised Arnold now has to admit that Robert was right about gentling the little wild cat.
The Little Lady Next Door is a 1915 short film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
After the Storm is a 1915 American short film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
It's a classic boy-meets-girl story, boy-loses-girl, boy gets mistaken for an escaped convict and ruthlessly chased by armies of cops across the countryside in a thrill-packed stunt-addled climax.
The story of a man -- accused of a crime he didn't commit and wounded by the posse -- who hides out on a desert ranch.

Blockade was one of those curious 1929 hybrids known as a "part-talkie." The story of a dauntless female prohibition agent. In her pursuit of a gang of Florida rum-runners, Bess assumes three identities. At various junctures, she is "herself," a society belle and a gangster's moll.
The Assayer of Lone Gap is a 1915 short film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
The Blot on the Shield is a 1915 short film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
The Bluffers is a 1915 American short film directed by B. Reeves Eason.

Pretty Dixie Chene is abut to be married to Slim Summerville besides a swimming pool stocked with baby alligators -- wait for it -- but before the minister shows up, Charles Murray and a drunken Polly Moran manage to cause quite a fuss.
Be My Wife is a 1919 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd.
The Man with the Punch is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by Edward Laemmle and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The New Superintendent is a 1911 American short drama film directed by Francis Boggs, featuring Hoot Gibson as an extra.
Imar the Servitor is a 1914 American silent drama film written by Daniel Carson Goodman. The film stars William Garwood.
His Nose in the Book is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by B. Reeves Eason and featuring Hoot Gibson.
Beautiful Bismark is a 1913 American silent short drama film starring William Garwood. It was released by Mutual Films.
Let's Go is a 1918 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd.
The Grinning Granger is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by Leo D. Maloney and featuring Hoot Gibson.

The hero befriends a young school teacher, who adopts a child at his suggestion. The real father of the child, who neglected its mother and allowed her to die, tries to make the teacher believe the hero is its father, which brings about an interesting complication.
Double Crossers is a 1921 American short silent Western film directed by William James Craft and featuring Hoot Gibson.
Hair Trigger Stuff is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by B. Reeves Eason and starring Hoot Gibson.
A young slum-reared fellow makes good with a man who befriends him and then sacrifices his good name to save the latter's son.
Crossed Clues is a 1921 American short silent Western film directed by William James Craft and featuring Hoot Gibson.
Why Pick on Me? is a 1918 short comedy film starring Harold Lloyd.
The Movie Trail is a 1921 American short silent Western film directed by Charles Thompson and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The Driftin' Kid is a 1921 American short silent Western film directed by Albert Russell and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The Man Who Woke Up is a 1921 American short silent Western film directed by Lee Kohlmar and featuring Hoot Gibson.
A young rancher rides away on a half-broken broncho. He is suspected of horse stealing and pursued, but retrieves his good name by saving a kidnapped girl and recovering stolen express funds.

A broken-down cowboy applies for work at one of the Western ranches. The boss agrees to hire the wanderer provided he can ride an unmanageable horse. He consents, rides the horse and gets the job. In accomplishing this "stunt," he arouses the jealousy of the foreman, for the latter learns that the ranchman's daughter has seen the new-comer subdue the wild animal and is beginning to fall in love with him. To prevent this the villain accuses his rival of many misdeeds, but in the end is a victim of his own folly.
The Wild Wild West is a 1921 American short silent Western film directed by Lee Kohlmar and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The Carnival Man is a 1929 American sound short drama film, directed by George Abbott and starring Walter Huston.

Hoot is the only cattleman in the neighborhood and he is about to be run off the range by the wealthiest sheep man in the district. Hoot is in love with the sheep man's daughter, and refuses to be run off. The little son of the sheep herder strays away and wanders to Hoot's shanty, where Hoot keeps him, sending a note to the father to come after him. A villainous foreman intercepts the note and plots a kidnapping frame-up. After a near tragic climax, Hoot captures and unmasks the villain, winning the girl and the good will of her father.
Courting Across the Court is a 1911 American silent short romantic comedy film. The film stars William Garwood.
The Cowboy and the Lady is a 1911 American silent Western film notable for being Alan Hale Sr.'s screen debut.
Cowpoke Sandy Adams overhears a plot to frame rancher Duncan McKenna for a rash of cattle rustlings and methodically turns the members of the gang against each other.
Wolf Tracks is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by Mack V. Wright and featuring Hoot Gibson.

A slicker sells a fake oil lease to Gertrude's father. Later the villain discovers that the lease is valuable, and to get it back he kidnaps the girl. Hoot rescues her in a thrilling fight on top of an oil derrick.
'In Wrong' Wright is a 1920 American silent Western film directed by Albert Russell and starring Hoot Gibson.

Ranchmen try to play a joke on one of their associates by signing his name to a letter addressed to Sarah Smith, who has advertised in a matrimonial journal. A mix-up occurs on the day of the arrival of the lady when a younger woman, sent to buy stock, also appears on the scene and is mistaken for the prospective bride.
The hero makes good with the bank president by preventing a robbery and thus wins the daughter's hand in marriage.
Hoot is a cowpuncher, somewhat addicted to liquor (when he can get it). His sweetheart, the rancher's daughter, tells him that if he ever takes another drink, their engagement is at an end.

Hector MacKnight, known to the townspeople as "Goofy" and an irritatingly terrible fiddler, is innocently drawn into a rigged poker game. A general fight brings the sheriff, and a chase ensues. Before the confusion is ended and Hector cleared, he meets Ruth Randolph and becomes involved in a circus while trying to recover the other half of her treasure map.
Soft Money is a 1919 American short comedy film featuring Harold Lloyd. The film is considered to be lost.

The girl is a school teacher in a cattle town, the hero a rather wild cowboy of good intentions but addicted to gambling. The girl saves him from a false accusation of robbery and this awakens his better instincts.
Beating the Game is a 1921 American silent Western film directed by Lee Kohlmar and featuring Hoot Gibson.
Bandits Beware is a 1921 American silent Western film directed by Lee Kohlmar and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The Fightin' Terror is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by and featuring Hoot Gibson.
Bianca is a 1913 silent American short film, written by Hanson Durham, and directed by Robert Thornby.
The Barren Gain is a 1915 American silent short drama film directed by Henry Otto and B. Reeves Eason.
The Shootin' Fool is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by and featuring Hoot Gibson.
Drawing the Line is a 1915 American short film directed by B. Reeves Eason and starring Vivian Rich.
Two Seats at the Opera is a 1916 American silent short comedy directed and starring William Garwood.
The Fightin' Fury is a 1921 American short silent Western film directed by and starring Hoot Gibson.
The Smilin' Kid is a 1920 American short silent Western film directed by and featuring Hoot Gibson.
The Exile of Bar-K Ranch is a 1915 American short silent Western film directed by B. Reeves Eason.
The Coffin Ship is a 1911 American silent short adventure film. The film starred William Garwood.

Roscoe is a family man at the seaside, lumbered with a shrewish wife and an extremely annoying young son. He meets up with a charming young lady in a bathing costume, and the two of them break into a charming and delightful dance. Unfortunately, the bathing beauty has a husband with pistols...
The Honor of the District Attorney is a 1915 American silent short film directed by Reaves Eason.
Our hero is a barber in a small Mexican town, wooing a local senorita, against the wishes of her mother.
